recipes.name: Vanilla Bean Cheesecake
ingredients_raw: 1 (18 ounce) package vanilla sandwich cookies (such as Oreo Golden Original Sandwich Cookies®)
1 vanilla bean, split lengthwise and seeds scraped

steps.text: Place oven racks on the bottom and middle positions; preheat the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C). Lightly butter a 10-inch springform pan.

Place sandwich cookies in a resealable plastic bag; crush with a rolling pin. Pour crumbs into a large bowl. Add scraped seeds of 1 vanilla bean; stir to combine. Drizzle crumbs with melted butter; stir to combine. Press into the bottom and up the sides of the prepared pan; set aside.

Beat cream cheese and sugar in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment on medium speed until smooth, about 3 minutes. Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. Add sour cream, heavy cream, remaining scraped seeds of 2 vanilla beans, and vanilla; beat on medium-high speed until blended and smooth, about 1 minute.
Pour cream cheese mixture into crust, leaving about 2 inches of space at the top of the pan for cake to expand as it bakes.

Place a baking dish on the bottom rack of the preheated oven; fill halfway with boiling water. Bake cheesecake on the middle rack until a small knife inserted into the center comes out clean, about 1 hour and 20 minutes.
Turn the oven off; let cheesecake cool inside the oven for 1 hour. Cover cheesecake with plastic wrap, then aluminum foil, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Vanilla Bean Cheesecake
raw_recipe.description: Three whole vanilla beans give this cheesecake telltale black specks of tropical flavor. This makes a big batch, so you can make some mini cheesecakes, too.

review.reviewBody: First, let me start by saying I make cheesecakes, a lot of them. Right now this is the reigning favorite. I follow the recipe other than: adding 4 vanilla beans, and I cook it a little differently. I cook all my cheesecakes the same, 325 degrees, in a water bath. To do this, wrap the bottom of your pan with a double layer of aluminum foil, place the springform pan in a roasting pan, then fill the pan with boiling water until it is half way up the side of your springform pan. Most importantly, your cheesecake is done when it jiggles slightly in the middle, don't wait until a knife comes out clean, it will be overdone. Then, place it on your counter after baking for about 30 minutes, then put into the refrigerator, uncovered for a few hours. Then wrap with plastic and let it set overnight, yes, you need to wait. This produces a perfectly baked, creamy, crack free cheesecake every time, regardless of the type of cheesecake. This one is super good, try it.

ELECTRIC PRESSURE COOKER VERSION! 

I didn't see a review so here is what I did to adapt.

I used a 7" springform pan in my 6 qt electric pressure cooker but it would have fit 8" easily. 

For this, I used about 7 oz of cookies for the crust
Half of all other ingredients except 3 eggs (instead of the 5 first called for)

I added 2 cups of water to the bottom of my PC, and a metal trivet. I put my PC on "warm" to preheat it while I prepped the ingredients. I poured the ingredients in all the way atop the crust-half of this recipe filled the 7" spring-form pan almost to the top. I took a long sheet of tin foil, folded triangles at the two ends, and placed the loaded spring-form pan on the foil, pinching the ends together as in a handle (like a triangle, cheesecake nestled on the bottom). Placed this in the PC, sealed it up, and placed it on high for 24 minutes. Allowed NATURAL RELEASE as it continues to cook during this time. It did not swell up noticeably, so don't worry about it overflowing into the pot.

Took out using the handles, still in place in the pot, and removed cheesecake. If there is any condensation on the top of the cake, gently blot with a napkin/papertowel. I allowed to cool at room temp and then bring down to fridge temp. Sets up fully once it's cold. Note: also took the half recipe and made two 7" versions - but cooked for 20 min each with natural release. Worked great too!

I've made this a few times and it has turned out awesome every time. It always makes too much for my 9" springform so last time I made a cupcake tray of cheesecake bites. 

Changes: Use half sugar. I read the suggestion from a couple commenters and this is a good one. Used 5 vanilla beans(total) instead of extract.

I've never used a traditional water bath but I place a dish filled with boiling water on the bottom rack. This has worked every time for THIS recipe. I always let the cheesecake cool off in the oven for an hourish, then pull it out and let it cool for another hour or so.

Delicious cheesecake! I followed the ingredients with the exception of the vanilla and vanilla beans. I added the beans from 4 pods and then added an extra tablespoon of vanilla extract. I also baked mine in a water bath just as a previous poster had mentioned! Turned out perfect with no cracks! Yay! My house smelled amazing! My daughter was delighted with her birthday cake! Thank you for a great recipe!

I absolutely loved this. I used 4 tsp of vanilla bean paste in the cake and opted for graham cracker crust the third time I made it. Cookies were a bit sweet for us. I did the water bath deal and it came out perfectly after about an hour at 325 (f). Thank you for this recipe, it’s a keeper!

My husband hates cheesecake and always begs me to make this one. I did omit the vanilla bean from the crust and just added it to the batter. I usually make mini cheesecakes (2in), and it is the perfect amount of batter and crust to make 48. It took me a while to figure out the temp and time I needed to cook the minis for, but I finally got it. I put a metal bowl of water on the bottom rack and cook on 300 degrees for 25 to 30 minutes. I only have one pan, so it takes a while, but it is worth it. I've started to make these for every party we have or go to. Everyone loves it!

My kids referred to this as the "ice cream" cheesecake since it was so creamy! I agreed with other bakers that using vanilla extract doesn't make sense so used 5 vanilla beans and omitted extract. Crust was very good but tended to crumble so may pre-bake next time. I baked as instructed and it came out crack-free! Would recommend ordering your vanilla beans online to avoid paying $$$ in stores. Definitely a keeper!

Made as directed only didn’t do the water thing in the oven just placed it on bottom rack and cranked up heat at the end to brown the top for the past @ 10 to about 375 . Everyone said it was the best cheesecake ever had!

this was great, but did do some changes - used 4 vanilla beans in the cream cheese mixture and left out the extract. I also used a graham cracker crust from the site instead of the cookies, but added one bean to that also, for a total of 5 beans used in the recipe. This recipe makes a lot of filling, I made one cheesecake, 12 minis in a cupcake pan and still threw a little cream cheese mixture away. I had to make 1 2/3 recipes for the graham cracker crust so I had enough for the minis also. cheesecake is great!!

Yum! Best cheesecake I've ever had! I only did a few things differently, I used kirkland vanilla (winnie the pooh) crackers for the crust and I used 3 tbsp of Madagascar bourbon pure Vanilla bean paste, in the filling only, I also didn't have heavy cream, so I used the melted butter mixed with milk trick. I will be making this again!

I made this for someone else so I didn't get to try it, but she said it was the best cheesecake she's ever tasted, period. The vanilla beans here are $10 each so I only used the two for the cake and didn't put any in the crust. I baked this in a water bath after encasing the pan in foil and it took 5 minutes longer than stated, probably just my oven. It turned out beautifully. The next day after chilling, I glazed it with chocolate ganache and splattered white and semisweet chocolate all over it, then masked it with a border of chocolate sprinkles. Very awesome looking in person! My cheesecake weighed in at 6 pounds!

I make cheesecakes frequently, and have for years. I give them to family and friends, take them to parties, etc., I made this one for a function in August and have been asked to make it three more times since then! I follow the recipe exactly, other than omitting the vanilla bean in the crust and adding them all to the filling. It turns out perfect every time! EVERYONE loves this cheesecake!
cut sugar in half and doubled the melted butter

This is a delicious cheesecake. I've made it many times for family and friends and for a variety of occasions ranging from holidays to the everyday . It's always a hit. To those people who make changes to the recipe, particularly multiple changes, you aren't making THIS recipe. You're creating new recipes. Thus, your reviews are meaningless. Perhaps your new versions are excellent. So why not post them as new recipes? Why critique this recipe that you aren't actually making? It's not fair to the person who created and posted this wonderful recipe. Please note that I'm not referring to people who add an extra vanilla bean or make some other minor change. I'm referring to people who alter the number of eggs plus the amount of sugar plus multiple other changes. You know who you are. So do we all. Your reviews are meaningless and unfair. If you can't or won't make the recipe as written and give an honest review of it, please don't downgrade it or criticize it. Just post your own recipe or move on.
Was easy and so full of flavor. Perfect, not too sweet.
love this recipe. i did not put the vanilla beans in the crust. save them for another cheesecake. my grandkids love this recipe
Very good recipe, the cheesecake is always a super success. However it needs to be said that the springform pan shouldn’t be removed till it’s completely cooled in the refrigerator.

I made this for my PT staff and it was delicious!! I took one persons advice and only used 2 vanilla beans in the cheesecake mix. I put vanilla extract into the crust. I would make this again for a special occasion because the vanilla beans are so expensive
I have been making this recipe for years.. and it’s very mind a fan favorite
Made this for coworkers birthday. Of all the things I’ve baked for them, this is definitely a favorite. I had extra filling so I filled a few ramekins and made some mini cheesecake magic!
